author: Grand Canyon Times
title: Crane introduces bill for increased transparency on TSA screening flaws
text:
Eli Crane, U.S. Representative from Arizona's 2nd Congressional District | Official U.S. House headshot
Eli Crane, U.S. Representative from Arizona's 2nd Congressional District | Official U.S. House headshot
Rep. Eli Crane of Arizona has introduced a bill aimed at increasing transparency regarding the Transportation Security Administration's (TSA) screening processes. The proposed legislation, known as the Aviation Risk Mitigation and Security (ARMS) Act, would mandate that the TSA report results from covert testing conducted at U.S. airports.
In 2015, a report by the Department of Homeland Security’s Office of Inspector General revealed that TSA officers using Advanced Imaging Technology (AIT) failed to detect concealed threat items 96% of the time. Following this revelation, the TSA ceased collecting and sharing data on these tests, opting instead to classify the information.
Rep. Crane emphasized the importance of Congress having access to up-to-date data to ensure that the TSA can effectively identify and neutralize threats. "I’m proud to introduce legislation requiring the TSA to provide Congress with updated covert testing data," he said. "In light of the legitimate security risks outlined in a recent DHS advisory bulletin, we cannot afford to remain in the dark about where the system is failing."
He further added that "the ARMS Act would strengthen congressional oversight and lay the groundwork for meaningful solutions." Rep. Crane urged his colleagues to support this measure, highlighting their duty to address longstanding deficiencies within the TSA.
